reasons.realCost: The real bill stays close to the sticker at every size tested: $129/mo for a solo user (the Core sticker itself), $149/mo for a small team, and $299/mo for a growing team against a $279 Growth sticker, because an extra seat costs only $20 a month.
reasons.pricingHonesty: Core and Growth plans and most add-ons are priced on the public pricing page, but that same page's Compare-plans table lists extra manager seats 'from $16' while SE Ranking's own Users FAQ states extra seats cost $20 per user per month, a direct conflict on the vendor's own site.
reasons.smallTeamFit: SE Ranking markets Core and Growth as self-serve plans for local-service businesses, freelancers and agencies, with only two main tiers to compare rather than a platform split across many separate add-on toolkits.
reasons.doesTheJob: Core and Growth cover rank tracking, site audits, backlink research, reporting and built-in AI-visibility tracking, with optional white-label and local-marketing add-ons, though its feature depth is generally positioned as a lighter alternative to larger platforms in the category.
reasons.freedomToLeave: Both plans can be billed monthly and canceled at any time, but SE Ranking deletes an account's data if a subscription is not renewed within 60 days of expiring, and its Agency Pack and API add-ons can only be bought on an annual subscription.
reasons.trackRecord: SE Ranking has operated since 2013 but retired its Essential, Pro and Business plans for new subscribers after an October 2024 pricing overhaul that introduced the current Core, Growth and Enterprise structure, and it is still migrating some accounts off its older 2Checkout billing system in 2026.

basis: SE Ranking gives the most predictable real bill and the simplest plan structure of the three for a small business, but a conflicting seat price on its own pricing page and a recent full pricing overhaul temper how much a buyer can rely on it staying stable.
method: Two separate AI passes (two runs of Anthropic's Claude over the same evidence, neither seeing the other's score) scored six factors (1–5) and an overall; published overall is the mean of the two overall scores, rounded down. Pass scores: 3.7 and 3.8.
